items.q: Why test models in your own app instead of trusting benchmarks?
items.a: Benchmarks give a rough idea, but you **only know a model in your own scenarios**.

items.q: Why should every AI app have model options?
items.a: New releases, price or **lost access** can force a switch, so keep the model a **one-line change**.

items.q: How did a prompt tweak fix Mistral's letter counting?
items.a: Asking it to **split into words, count per word and sum** with reasoning got the right answer.

items.q: How do you test RAG groundedness?
items.a: Ask a **half-answerable question**; a grounded model **admits what the sources don't cover**.

items.q: What do weaker models do when sources have gaps?
items.a: They **fill gaps from their weights** and present it as if it came from the context.

items.q: What do wrong tool arguments usually reveal?
items.a: **Ambiguity in your tool descriptions**; tighten them and re-run the cases.

items.q: What helper tool should LLM apps get for dates?
items.a: A **date math tool**, because models are bad at date arithmetic, **especially leap years**.

items.q: Besides the answer, what separates models in a tool loop?
items.a: **Efficiency**: how many calls they need, e.g. **one batched calculation** vs four calls.

items.q: What are parallel tool calls good for?
items.a: Running **independent steps in the same turn**, like flight and hotel search, to **cut latency**.

items.q: What agent failure did Mistral show?
items.a: It **stopped before the final step**, so check that **every required step** is completed.

items.q: What is the simplest eval for a single tool call?
items.a: A **string check** on the **tool name and arguments**.

items.q: What should an LLM judge return?
items.a: **Pass or fail plus a reason**, given the query, response and **full context or traces**.

items.q: Which built-in evaluators are not worth running?
items.a: **Coherence and fluency**; build **custom evaluators** for your app instead.

items.q: What does DSPy with GEPA change?
items.a: Your **spec and checks become the code** and the **prompt is the output**, so cheaper models can pass.
